concerns.description: The Risks bullet says mark stripping "affects scripts such as Devanagari". The stripped range \u0300-\u036f covers only Combining Diacritical Marks, and Devanagari marks lie outside it. Replace the example with scripts that are affected and already dropped by [^a-z0-9], such as Cyrillic й or Greek ά, so the stated premise is true.
The Performance NFR says "4 linear passes", but the chain has five operations: normalize, replace, toLowerCase and two replace calls. Correct it to five, or drop the count and keep "O(n)".

FR-0 requires tests 7 / pass 7 / fail 0, but after commit 1 alone npm test can only report tests 2 / pass 2. The spec never says which commit carries the 5 new tests. State FR-0's acceptance as 2/2 at commit 1 and 7/7 at commit 2, and assign the new tests to commit 2 with the fix, so each commit has a checkable gate.

FR-5 is traced only to "review of the comment diff", which is neither a named test nor a command. Replace it with a command, for example grep -niE 'empty|accent' src/slug.js returning no gap lines and grep -nE 'ß|ligature' src/slug.js returning the new gap lines.

summary: The design is sound and minimal, but two factual errors (the Devanagari claim and the pass count) and two traceability gaps (FR-0's commit-dependent count and FR-5's review-only proof) must be fixed before resubmission; the absence of CI is out of scope.
